provenance.notes: Researched definition in tools/extract/patterns/src/extra-2.mjs. Bindings are cited but not all checked against a primary source; roles and key names are cross-checked mechanically against apg-skeleton.json and aria-roles.json. Arabic name is an unreviewed translation.

roles.on: the top-level items and each panel's links
trigger that shows a panel of links
roles.note: A disclosure button, not a menuitem.

attributes.name: aria-label
attributes.values: name of the navigation; or aria-labelledby

keyboard.action: Move through triggers, links and the links of an open panel in page order. Tabbing out of the navigation closes the open panel.
On a trigger: toggle its panel; opening one closes any other. On a link: Enter follows it.
Close the open panel and return focus to its trigger.
Move focus to the next top-level trigger or link.
Move focus to the previous top-level trigger or link.
On an open trigger of a horizontal bar: move focus into its panel. Inside a panel: next link.
Move focus to the first item of the current level.
Move focus to the last item of the current level.

focus.entry: Every trigger and link is a tab stop.
focus.exit: Tab; leaving closes the open panel.
focus.restore: Escape returns focus to the trigger.
focus.tabStops: One per top-level item, plus the links of the open panel, which follow their trigger in the tab order even when rendered elsewhere.

variants: menubar navigation (role menubar; see menubar): only for application-like menus
vertical (sidebar) with ArrowRight entering a panel

rtlDecisions.question: In a horizontal roving-focus composite (tabs, toolbar, menubar, radio group, toggle group), which arrow moves to the next item in RTL?
rtlDecisions.apg: Silent, apart from one aside in the tabs page that calls the last tab the right-most "in a left-to-right horizontal tab list". Keys are named physically: Right Arrow is next.

libraries.behaviour: ArrowLeft is next in RTL for tabs, toolbar and horizontal radio groups; vertical arrows never flip.
The composite root swaps the forward and backward horizontal keys when direction is rtl.
The roving focus group swaps ArrowLeft and ArrowRight before mapping a key to a focus intent when dir is rtl; toggle group, tabs, toolbar, radio group and menubar all pass dir through it.
Tabs and ToggleButtonGroup pass isRtl to the roving tabindex root.
Tabs flip the arrow offset when rtl and the tab bar is top or bottom; a horizontal menu maps Left to next when rtl.

rtlDecisions.reason: Items are laid out from inline-start, so the arrow that points at the visually following item must move to it. All five libraries agree.

rtlDecisions.question: Which arrow opens a submenu from a vertical menu, and which closes it, in RTL?
rtlDecisions.apg: Silent. No pattern page mentions right-to-left; keys are described physically (left, right) for a left-to-right layout. Right Arrow opens a submenu, Left Arrow closes it.

libraries.behaviour: In RTL ArrowLeft opens the submenu and ArrowRight closes it.
SUB_OPEN_KEYS and SUB_CLOSE_KEYS are keyed by direction: rtl opens with ArrowLeft, closes with ArrowRight.
List navigation takes an rtl flag; the cross-orientation open and close keys are ArrowLeft and ArrowRight respectively when rtl.
In a vertical menu Left means "children" (open) and Right means "parent" (close) when rtl.

rtlDecisions.reason: A submenu opens toward inline-end, which is the left in RTL; the arrow must point where the submenu appears.

data.notes: Site navigation is links and disclosure buttons, not ARIA menus: Tab stays in page order and arrows are an optional extra. Radix and Base UI add the arrows; both are direction-aware (read from source): in a horizontal bar the previous-item key is ArrowRight in RTL, and in a vertical bar the key that enters a panel is ArrowLeft in RTL instead of ArrowRight. That vertical entry key is the submenu rule; it is described here in notes rather than bound, because we ship the horizontal bar first.
